The last graph shows no particular batch effect in the control strains (DGY1315, 500, 3183). This allows us to do comparisons across batches. What I want to do here is to find, at every FLC conc, the ratio of the growth rate of a given CNV strain to that of the avg across all control strains.

```{r ratioplot_prep}

#Avg of control strains across batches
Controlmeans=aggregate(Commonconcs_goodbatches_control$r,list(Commonconcs_goodbatches_control$FLC_conc),mean)

#Getting CNV data separately
Commonconcs_goodbatches_CNV=Commonconcs_goodbatches[Commonconcs_goodbatches$Type!="Control",]
Commonconcs_goodbatches_CNV$Growthrate_ratio=0

#CNVstrainnames=unique(Commonconcs_goodbatches_CNVstrains_output$Strain)

l=length(Commonconcs_goodbatches_CNV$FLC_conc)

for (i in (1:l)) {
  relconc=Commonconcs_goodbatches_CNV$FLC_conc[i]
  relvalue=Controlmeans$x[Controlmeans$Group.1==relconc]
  Commonconcs_goodbatches_CNV$Growthrate_ratio[i]=Commonconcs_goodbatches_CNV$r[i]/relvalue
}

```

This part written with the help of MAI-Code-1-Flash on 6/24/26, and manually modified.
```{r MAI_ttest}
strainnames <- unique(Commonconcs_goodbatches_CNV$Strain)
results <- list()

for (s in strainnames) {
  for (c in unique(Commonconcs_goodbatches_CNV$FLC_conc)) {
    tmp <- subset(
      Commonconcs_goodbatches_CNV,
      Strain == s & FLC_conc == c & !is.na(Growthrate_ratio)
    )
    #str(tmp$Growthrate_ratio)
    #print(tmp$Growthrate_ratio)
    #tmp2=sd(tmp$Growthrate_ratio, na.rm = TRUE)
    #print(tmp2)

    if (nrow(tmp) >= 2) {
      tt <- t.test(tmp$Growthrate_ratio, mu = 1)
      
      fev <- unique(tmp$FLC_evolved)
      fev <- if (length(fev) == 1) fev[1] else NA
      
      results[[length(results) + 1]] <- data.frame(
        Strain = s,
        FLC_conc = c,
        FLC_evolved = fev,
        n = nrow(tmp),
        estimate = as.numeric(tt$estimate),
        p.value = tt$p.value,
        t.stat=tt$statistic,
        conf.low = tt$conf.int[1],
        conf.high = tt$conf.int[2]
      )
    }
  }
}

test_results <- do.call(rbind, results)
test_results

write.csv(test_results,"ttest_CNV.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

## Variance within vs between CNV strains (appended 10/28/26)

Using only strains with Type=="CNV" (this excludes the engineered strains), at each FLC conc, I ask whether growth rate varies more *between* strains (differences among CNV strains) or *within* a strain (replicate-to-replicate variation). Growthrate_ratio is used (r divided by the control mean at the same FLC conc), so conc-specific differences in overall growth do not get mixed into the variance.

Approach: at each FLC conc, a one-way random-effects ANOVA with Strain as the grouping factor. The F-test (MS between / MS within) asks whether between-strain variance exceeds within-strain variance. Variance components are estimated from the mean squares, with the unbalanced-design correction n0 because replicate numbers differ across strains. ICC = between / (between + within), i.e. the fraction of total variance explained by strain identity.

```{r variance_prep}
CNV_only = Commonconcs_goodbatches_CNV_ordered[Commonconcs_goodbatches_CNV_ordered$Type=="CNV" & !is.na(Commonconcs_goodbatches_CNV_ordered$Growthrate_ratio),]
CNV_only$Strain = factor(CNV_only$Strain)

#Replicates per strain per conc
table(CNV_only$Strain, CNV_only$FLC_conc)

variance_components = function(df) {
  df$Strain = droplevels(df$Strain)
  a = nlevels(df$Strain)
  N = nrow(df)
  ni = table(df$Strain)
  tab = anova(lm(Growthrate_ratio ~ Strain, data = df))
  MSB = tab["Strain","Mean Sq"]
  MSW = tab["Residuals","Mean Sq"]
  n0 = (N - sum(ni^2)/N)/(a - 1)   #effective replicates per strain, unbalanced design
  var_between = max((MSB - MSW)/n0, 0)
  var_within = MSW
  data.frame(
    n_strains = a,
    n_obs = N,
    var_within = var_within,
    var_between = var_between,
    sd_within = sqrt(var_within),
    sd_between = sqrt(var_between),
    ICC = var_between/(var_between + var_within),
    F_value = tab["Strain","F value"],
    df1 = tab["Strain","Df"],
    df2 = tab["Residuals","Df"],
    p_value = tab["Strain","Pr(>F)"]
  )
}

variance_results = CNV_only %>%
  group_by(FLC_conc) %>%
  group_modify(~ variance_components(.x)) %>%
  ungroup()

variance_results$p_adj_BH = p.adjust(variance_results$p_value, method = "BH")
as.data.frame(variance_results)

#write.csv(variance_results, "variance_within_between_CNV.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

Plots: (1) growth rate ratio for each strain at each conc, to see spread within strains relative to spread among strain means; (2) within vs between SD per conc.

## Is between-strain variability greater than within-strain variability? (CNV strains, FLC_conc != 0)

Question: among CNV strains grown in fluconazole, is the variance between strains greater than the variance within a strain?

Model (Growthrate_ratio, CNV strains, FLC_conc != 0): conc is a fixed effect, and Strain and Strain:conc are random effects. Between-strain variance = Var(Strain) + Var(Strain:conc), i.e. strain differences both overall and conc-specific. Within-strain variance = residual variance (replicate-to-replicate variation).

Test statistic: variance ratio = between / within. Between > within corresponds to a ratio > 1. The ratio is not analytically testable, so a parametric bootstrap of the fitted model gives its sampling distribution: a 95% CI, and an approximate one-sided p-value for H0: ratio <= 1 (the proportion of bootstrap ratios <= 1).

```{r between_vs_within_test, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
CNV_only = Commonconcs_goodbatches_CNV_ordered[Commonconcs_goodbatches_CNV_ordered$Type=="CNV",]
CNV_only$Strain = factor(CNV_only$Strain)

BW_data = CNV_only[CNV_only$FLC_conc != 0, ]
BW_data$Strain = droplevels(BW_data$Strain)
BW_data$conc_f = factor(BW_data$FLC_conc)

BW_fit = lmer(Growthrate_ratio ~ conc_f + (1 | Strain) + (1 | Strain:conc_f), data = BW_data)
print(VarCorr(BW_fit))

#Between / within variance ratio from a fitted model
bw_ratio = function(m) {
  vc = as.data.frame(VarCorr(m))
  between = sum(vc$vcov[vc$grp %in% c("Strain", "Strain:conc_f")])
  within = vc$vcov[vc$grp == "Residual"]
  between / within
}

observed_ratio = bw_ratio(BW_fit)

nsim = 2000
BW_boot = bootMer(BW_fit, bw_ratio, nsim = nsim, type = "parametric", seed = 1)
boot_ratios = BW_boot$t[, 1]

cat("Observed between/within variance ratio:", observed_ratio, "\n")
cat("95% bootstrap CI for the ratio:", quantile(boot_ratios, c(0.025, 0.975)), "\n")
cat("Approx. one-sided p-value (H0: between <= within):", (sum(boot_ratios <= 1) + 1) / (nsim + 1), "\n")

hist(boot_ratios, breaks = 50, main = "Parametric bootstrap: between / within variance", xlab = "Variance ratio (between / within)")
abline(v = 1, lty = 2)
abline(v = observed_ratio, col = "red")
```

Interpretation: if the 95% CI for the ratio lies entirely above 1 (and the p-value is small), between-strain variability is greater than within-strain variability. If the CI includes 1, the data cannot distinguish the two. A message about a singular fit means one of the between-strain variances was estimated at 0, which pulls the ratio down.
